Thought: Let me recall the flammability properties of these compounds:

1. Metal hydrides (like NaH, LiH): These compounds react vigorously with water to produce hydrogen gas, which is highly flammable. Many metal hydrides can ignite spontaneously in air.

2. Metal alkyls (like trimethylaluminum): These are organometallic compounds that are extremely reactive. Many metal alkyls ignite spontaneously when exposed to air without any ignition source.

3. Metal aryls (like phenyllithium): Similar to metal alkyls, these organometallic compounds are highly reactive and many can ignite spontaneously in air.

4. Silanes (like SiH4): These silicon-hydrogen compounds are also extremely reactive and many silanes can ignite spontaneously when exposed to air.

The key characteristic of these compounds is that they can ignite spontaneously in air without an external ignition source. This property is described as "pyrophoric" - materials that ignite spontaneously at or below 54°C (130°F) in air.

So these compounds would be classified as pyrophoric rather than just highly flammable or combustible. "Nonflammable" is definitely incorrect.
